title: ACF conformance matrix
description: AgentCE's own scorecard input for the Agent Conformance Framework: one entry per named ACF capability, each with a natural-language statement of what level 3 means and, where a capability is verifiable today, an executable test. This is an internal QA artifact of the conformance suite, not a spec vocabulary schema -- it carries no canonical agent-conformance.org IRI and is not vendored into the three engines.

id.description: Stable capability id, e.g. COV-1. The dimension-prefix letters are informative only; `dimension` is the field a consumer must read.

dimension.description: One of the ACF's seven named dimensions (the framework document's 'The seven dimensions' section, in that same order).

capability.description: The named sub-capability exactly as it appears in the framework document's dimension bullet (e.g. 'Standards & rulesets').

statement.description: Natural-language statement of what 'covered at level 3 (Complete)' means for a user, for this capability. Self-documenting test definition -- read this to know what the test proves.

level_target.description: The level this entry's test (when present) proves on a pass. 0=Absent, 1=Asserted, 2=Partial, 3=Complete, per the ACF maturity scale. An entry with no `test` always scores 1 (Asserted) regardless of this field, by the scorer's own anti-hype rule.

cmd.description: One shell command, run from the repository root, that discriminates: exit 0 (and, if `expect` is set, producing output containing `expect`) iff the capability is real at `level_target` today.

fixture.description: The input path the test operates over -- a corpus fixture, a spec/catalog directory, or a repository-level artifact (a doc, a workflow file, a schema). Null when the test needs no fixture input (e.g. it drives an installed CLI against ambient repository state).

expect.description: A substring the command's combined stdout+stderr must contain on success, beyond a zero exit code. Null when the exit code alone is the signal.

evidence_ref.description: Required (non-null) when `level_target` is 3: a human-readable pointer (file path, CI job, or doc anchor) a reader can follow to see the proof, distinct from `test.cmd` which a machine runs.
